column3: Two outside the family. *** "Lisa", Australia, 23.0 cM across 2 segments, tree of 177 - shared ancestral surnames BRAYLEY and BAKER. *** And *** "Ron Brayley", United Kingdom, 16.2 cM across 2 segments *** - shared ancestral surname BRAYLEY. Both estimated 5th cousin.
column4: *** THE BRAYLEY LINE IS IN THE DNA. *** Two independent matches, one of them carrying the surname himself, and MyHeritage computing BRAYLEY as common to their trees and Cheryl's - which also proves the Brayley line is in her MyHeritage tree, exactly as the GEDCOM said.

finding
*** THE BAILEY CLUSTER IS NOT SHOWN TO BE THE BRAYLEY LINE. ***
column2: Cluster 14 - three matches, 61 to 116 cM, all BAILEY trees, all USA - *** did not appear in the Brayley search at all. *** None of the three carries Brayley as an ancestral surname.

column1: *** AND THAT ABSENCE PROVES NOTHING EITHER. ***
column2: *** Their trees hold TWO people and FOUR people. *** MyHeritage cannot compute a shared ancestral surname from a tree with two people in it. So their absence from the Brayley result is *** uninformative, not contrary. ***

column1: *** THE HONEST POSITION. ***
column2: *** The Bailey-to-Brayley link is UNTESTED, not refuted - and this archive said "probably" this morning when it had no business to. *** The real Brayley and Temple matches sit at 14 to 25 cM, in the United Kingdom, Australia, the USA and South Africa. The Bailey cluster sits at 61 to 116 cM in the USA. *** They are different signals at different distances, and nothing yet joins them. ***
